what_this_is: A new operator, with no account, doing the whole job through the dashboard in a real browser: register a tenant, create an agent, grant it authority, take its credential, watch a real agent process use that authority against the live gateway, approve one action as a human, read the evidence, then revoke.
how_it_was_driven: Chromium via Playwright against the built frontend, clicking the same controls a person would. Nothing was called directly; the browser was the only client.
the_agent: A container on aegis_agent_net holding nothing but the credential the wizard displayed. It is a separate process from the seeded demo agent, and it was started after the credential was issued, from that credential alone.

first_two_runs_failed_honestly: Runs ea65ad1d and c32dfd83 report 11/12. The failing check is 'approved action executes after a human grants it', and it failed because no human approved within the agent's 90-second window: the first time the driver script crashed before approving, the second time it approved the earlier run's still-pending request instead of the new one. Aegis did the right thing both times, and reported FAIL rather than passing an unapproved action. They are kept here rather than deleted, because a suite that only ever shows the clean run is not evidence.
